extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and publishing news about military operations, official communiqués, and government statements during wartime, with emphasis on verification, attribution and operational-security caution. The piece exemplifies AP-style coverage of battlefield developments, political reactions, and official messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold operational details while battle continues
rubrics_metrics.description: “No details will be reported while the battle continues. To announce details of these actions while the battle is in progress would furnish the enemy with information of definite value to him.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish specific tactical details about ongoing engagements (ship movements, precise losses, positions) because releasing such information could aid the enemy; delay or withhold sensitive details until the engagement is over or officially cleared for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag unconfirmed enemy or partisan claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Enemy or partisan broadcasts and communiqués (e.g., Tokyo’s claims of sinkings) are presented with caution and explicitly noted as unconfirmed: “This was the customary Nazi Saturday communique ... and was not confirmed from other sources.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting claims originating from enemy state media or partisan sources, label them clearly as claims and state whether independent confirmation exists; avoid presenting such claims as established fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute information to its source
rubrics_metrics.description: The article consistently identifies sources: radio broadcasts, official communiqués, statements “By the Associated Press,” and named spokesmen or governments (e.g., “the Vichy radio reported,” “Reliable quarters in London declared”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always attribute statements, reports and allegations to their originating source so readers can assess provenance and reliability; specify when information comes from official communiqués, broadcasts, spokesmen, or unnamed 'reliable quarters.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify authenticity of proclamations and report verification status
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece distinguishes between authenticated and disputed messages (e.g., "Reliable quarters in London declared that Darlan’s pro-American proclamation ... undoubtedly was genuine" and later references to subsequent repudiation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek corroboration for major proclamations or dramatic political turns; when authenticity is confirmed, report that confirmation; when authenticity is in doubt, report that doubt and any conflicting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish full texts of important official messages when available
rubrics_metrics.description: The article prints the text of President Roosevelt’s message to the Governor General of Algeria and other official messages, noting when publication was withheld until receipt was confirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an important official message is available and its authenticity/receipt is verified, publish the full text (or substantial excerpts) and note any decision to delay publication pending confirmation, so readers can see primary material and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish propaganda-influenced communiqués from neutral official statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases such as “The Vichy expressions, carried as official French communiques but doubtless inspired by Germans” mark certain statements as likely influenced by external (propaganda) forces rather than purely domestic government policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and explain when official-sounding releases may be influenced by occupying powers or propaganda, and avoid treating such releases as independent or unbiased government positions without scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undue speculation — present interpretations as such
rubrics_metrics.description: The article asks questions and proposes hypotheses cautiously (e.g., "Why such a small incident should be made the subject of a formal communique was not clear, but Allied quarters thought it might have been broadcast for exemplary purposes").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offering explanations or interpreting motives, clearly label them as speculation or opinion and, where possible, provide alternative explanations and the source of the interpretation (e.g., 'Allied quarters thought...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear chronological and geographic context
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports include dates, local time references, locations (e.g., Solomon Islands, North Africa, Guadalcanal), and sequences of events to situate developments in time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise dates, times (or time-zone context), and locations for military and political events to help readers understand the timeline and geographical setting of reported actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note when information is omitted or limited by authority or security
rubrics_metrics.description: The communique’s explanation for withholding details (“To announce details...would furnish the enemy with information of definite value to him”) and references to withheld publication until receipt confirmation show editorial restraint imposed by security or official decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material is omitted, delayed, or constrained for security or official reasons, explicitly state that limitation and, if possible, explain the reason (e.g., operational security, awaiting confirmation) so readers understand reporting gaps.
